title: ClarkAtlanta vs MorganState: control, tuition, size
summary: Clark Atlanta University (ClarkAtlanta) versus Morgan State University (MorganState). Also searched as MorganState vs ClarkAtlanta. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Clark Atlanta University and Morgan State University differ notably in several aspects. Clark Atlanta University is a private nonprofit institution located in Atlanta, while Morgan State University is a public university based in Baltimore. The undergraduate enrollment at Clark Atlanta is approximately 3,603 students, compared to Morgan State's larger undergraduate population of about 9,019. Tuition costs also vary significantly; Clark Atlanta's in-state tuition is $28,310, whereas Morgan State offers a lower in-state tuition rate of $8,229. These differences highlight the distinct profiles of the two universities in terms of ownership, size, location, and cost.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing Clark Atlanta University and Morgan State University in terms of cost, there are significant differences. Clark Atlanta University charges $28,310 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition, reflecting its status as a private institution. In contrast, Morgan State University, a public university, has an in-state tuition of $8,229 and an out-of-state tuition of $19,124. Despite the disparity in tuition fees, the median debt for students who complete their degrees is relatively similar, with Clark Atlanta graduates carrying a median debt of $27,000 and Morgan State graduates having a median debt of $27,250. These figures illustrate the varying financial commitments required by students attending each university.
